subject: biology
title: Animal Coordination & Homeostasis
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Animal Coordination & Homeostasis — how hormones and the nervous system keep the body in balance.
meta_desc: GCSE Biology on hormones, the endocrine system and homeostasis.
final_note: You walked through 's coordination and homeostasis course points.

concepts.def: Keeping internal conditions within a narrow range
Chemical messenger released by a gland into blood
Network of glands that secrete hormones
Master gland in the brain controlling other glands
Organ a hormone acts on via specific receptors
Response reversing a change from normal levels

walkthroughs.body_html:
Nerves are fast and short-lived; hormones are slower and longer-lasting.

Nerves use electrical impulses. Hormones travel in the bloodstream from gland to target organ.

Body temperature, blood glucose and water balance are kept steady. If a value rises, a response is triggered to lower it.

This negative feedback is the core idea of homeostasis.

mcqs.q: Hormones travel around the body in the:
options: Bloodstream
Nerves
Lymph nodes
Air sacs

mcqs.q: What does negative feedback do in homeostasis?
options: Negative feedback makes a process get worse or amplifies the change.
Negative feedback stops the body from responding to any internal change.
Hormones are released directly into target organs by being injected by glands.
It reverses a change in a controlled variable, bringing it back towards the set point.

mcqs.q: How do hormones reach their target organs?
options: They are carried in the bloodstream and act on cells with specific receptors for that hormone.
Hormones are released directly into target organs by being injected by glands.
Negative feedback stops the body from responding to any internal change.
Hormones are sent through nerves directly to specific organs.

mcqs.q: How does sweating help cool you down?
options: Sweating removes excess heat by carrying it out as liquid waste.
Hormones are released directly into target organs by being injected by glands.
Evaporation of sweat absorbs energy (latent heat) from the skin, lowering body temperature.
Sweat is cold and directly cools the skin on contact.

mcqs.q: When body temperature rises, blood vessels near the skin surface widen (vasodilation). How does this help cool the body?
options: More blood flows near the surface, so more heat is lost.
Less blood reaches the surface, trapping heat.
The blood vessels move to the skin surface.
It increases respiration to make more heat.

mcqs.q: A person's blood glucose falls below normal. Which hormone is released and what does it do?
options: Glucagon, which raises blood glucose
Insulin, which raises blood glucose
Glucagon, which lowers blood glucose
Insulin, which lowers blood glucose

Carried along neurones

mcqs.q: Thyroxine controls the body's metabolic rate. Its level is kept steady by negative feedback, which means a rise in thyroxine will:
options: Reduce further release of thyroxine
Increase release of thyroxine further
Have no effect on its release
Stop all metabolism completely

free_texts.q: What is the name for keeping internal conditions stable? One word, lowercase.

sequence.def: A factor moves above or below its normal level
Brain or gland processes the information
Muscle or gland acts to oppose the change
The factor moves back toward the set point
Normal level restored; response switches off
